zones.what: Lifeboats mounted at Deck 5 obstruct views from Deck 5 cabins completely and partially obstruct ocean views from Deck 8 and lower Deck 9 cabins, though horizon remains visible.
zones.effect: Deck 5 ocean-view cabins look directly into or over orange lifeboat shells; Deck 8 ocean views are partially blocked especially when looking down; low Deck 9 balconies may see boat tops at the edge of view.
zones.mattersTo: Critical for anyone who wants unobstructed water views or photos; less important if you spend little time in the cabin or prefer the lower price point.

zones.what: Deck 11 Orchestra Restaurant (main dining room) sits directly above aft Deck 10 and two decks above aft Deck 9.
zones.effect: Dinner service noise—chair scraping, footfall, occasional dropped items—filters down during evening hours, roughly 6pm to 10:30pm across two seatings.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers or anyone in the cabin during dinner hours; irrelevant if you're out exploring the ship in the evenings.

zones.what: Deck 11 and Deck 12 public venues (L'Oleandro Restaurant forward, buffet and pools mid-ship) sit above forward and mid Deck 10.
zones.effect: Daytime and evening foot traffic, pool deck activity, and buffet service create intermittent noise overhead; most active roughly 7am to 11pm.
zones.mattersTo: Affects light sleepers and anyone wanting afternoon naps; less relevant for guests who are rarely in cabins during the day.

zones.what: Theater Deck (Deck 7) sits two decks below forward Deck 9; showtime vibration and bass can carry upward during evening performances.
zones.effect: Low-frequency sound from shows (typically 8pm and 10pm) may be faintly perceptible, though significantly dampened by two deck layers.
zones.mattersTo: Mainly concerns extremely noise-sensitive guests; most won't notice or will be at the show themselves.

zones.what: Deck 9 cabins sit directly overhead mid and aft Deck 8 cabins (standard guest cabin construction).
zones.effect: Normal footfall, drawer closing, and conversation from the cabin above audible with typical cruise ship soundproofing; most noticeable early morning and late evening.
zones.mattersTo: Sensitive sleepers may prefer top cabin deck (Deck 10) to avoid overhead neighbors; most guests find it tolerable background.

zones.what: Elevator banks run forward, mid-ship, and aft on all cabin decks with machinery noise and passenger traffic at landings.
zones.effect: Cabins immediately adjacent to elevator lobbies hear mechanical hum, door chimes, and conversation as guests wait; cabins one or two doors away gain convenience without most noise.
zones.mattersTo: Mobility-limited guests benefit from proximity despite noise; light sleepers should avoid immediate-adjacent cabins.

zones.what: Deck 5 aft section sits relatively low and toward stern, closer to propulsion machinery zones.
zones.effect: Low-frequency vibration may be perceptible underway, particularly at higher speeds; typically felt as subtle hum through floor and bed frame.
zones.mattersTo: Vibration-sensitive guests should avoid; those who sleep through anything or like the engine hum as white noise won't mind.

zones.what: Bow thruster machinery operates in forward sections during docking and maneuvering, and anchor chain deploys through hawsepipe during port arrivals.
zones.effect: Loud mechanical grinding from thrusters during port arrival/departure (5-15 minutes); anchor chain roar early morning in port (brief but startling if asleep).
zones.mattersTo: Critical for light sleepers who value quiet mornings in port; non-issue for early risers or those who sleep through noise.
